newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian police to swap old trousers for jeans.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian police to swap old trousers for jeans.

text.p: Bavarian police will soon be moving with the times and stepping out in jeans to enforce law and order, the southern state's Interior Ministry said on Thursday.

From this spring denim -- albeit beige-coloured and not classic blue -- will replace the more conservative material used in the old-style trousers. The new trousers will not only be more fashionable but probably cheaper.
The Interior Ministry said they had decided on the change because jeans had become generally acceptable in most areas of public life in Germany.
Police officers said they were delighted with the idea.
The new trousers, with five pockets and a smart crease down the middle of the leg, will be worn with the normal uniform jacket, also beige, the ministry said.
Blue jeans combined with a jacket and tie are considered smart enough for work in many jobs in Germany.
